paragraphs.text: Familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (FHL) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by hyperactive phagocytes and defects in natural killer (NK) cell function (zur Stadt et al., 2005). It presents as a severe hyperinflammatory syndrome with activated macrophages and T lymphocytes and affects young children (Zur Stadt et al., 2006). Compared with other forms of FHL, FHL4 has been associated with a milder course, including long disease-free remissions without specific treatment, although some affected children develop severe psychomotor retardation, myelodysplastic syndrome, or acute myelogenous leukemia (Rudd et al., 2006).

paragraphs.text: Muller et al. (2014) reported 3 patients from 3 unrelated consanguineous Pakistani families who presented with HLH: 2 boys diagnosed at 2 months and 5 years of age and a girl diagnosed at 48 months. Only patient B had a family history of the disease. Patients A and B had fever, splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, anemia (hemoglobin 55 and 71 g/L), neutropenia (0.3 and 0.4 x 10(9)/L), thrombocytopenia (13 and 8 x 10(9)/L), hypertriglyceridemia (5.1 and 5.5 mmol/L), hypofibrinogenemia (0.28 and 0.16 g/L), and hyperferritinemia (8,636 and 1,929 microg/L). Hemophagocytosis was not observed in either patient, and neither had neurologic manifestations. Clinical data at presentation could not be retrieved for patient C. All 3 patients had deficient NK cell cytotoxicity and degranulation. Patients A and B were treated with dexamethasone, cyclosporine A, and etoposide and were in remission at 2 months. Patient A underwent hematopoietic stem cell transplantation at 15 months; both patients A and B died. Patient C was lost to follow-up.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a large consanguineous Kurdish kindred with FHL4 mapped to chromosome 6q24, zur Stadt et al. (2005) screened positional candidate genes and identified a homozygous 5-bp deletion in the STX11 gene. Syntaxin-11 protein was absent from the mononuclear cell fraction of patients homozygous for the deletion. zur Stadt et al. (2005) also found homozygous STX11 mutations in 5 other consanguineous Turkish/Kurdish FHL kindreds: the 5-bp deletion in 2 families, a large 19.2-kb genomic deletion spanning the entire coding region of STX11 (exon 2) in 1 family, and a nonsense mutation leading to a premature stop codon in the C-terminal end of the protein in 2 families. Because both STX11 and UNC13D are involved in vesicle trafficking and membrane fusion, the authors concluded that defects in the endocytotic or exocytotic pathway may be a common mechanism in FHL.

paragraphs.text: In 3 patients with FHL4 from 3 unrelated consanguineous Pakistani families, Muller et al. (2014) sequenced the coding regions and splice sites of UNC13D, STX11, and STXBP2. All 3 patients were homozygous for a missense mutation in STX11 (L58P). The parents were heterozygous for the mutation. Patient A also carried a heterozygous UNC13D variant (P271S) and a homozygous UNC13D variant (R928C). This patient presented at a younger age than the other 2 patients and showed less restoration of NK cell degranulation after IL-2 stimulation, and the authors suggested that the UNC13D variants may have contributed to the severity of his disease. Syntaxin-11 expression was greatly reduced in PBMCs and LAK cells from patient C, whereas Munc18-2 expression was normal. In transfected HEK293T cells, the L58P mutant was expressed at levels similar to wildtype but did not bind Munc18-2.

paragraphs.text: Muller et al. (2014) found that NK cells from patients homozygous for the STX11 L58P mutation had defective lysis of K562 target cells and defective degranulation in response to K562 cells or CD16 engagement. Both functions were partially restored by IL-2 stimulation. Expression of perforin, granzyme B, and CD107a was normal, indicating that granule integrity was not impaired. In pull-down experiments, both the patient-derived L58P mutation in the Habc domain and an engineered mutation in the N-terminal peptide (R4A) abolished binding of syntaxin-11 to Munc18-2, whereas the C-terminal Q268X mutant still bound Munc18-2. The authors concluded that both the N terminus and the Habc domain of syntaxin-11 are needed to bind Munc18-2, and suggested that loss of this interaction may destabilize syntaxin-11 and explain the low levels of the mutant protein in patient cells.

checks.claim: Muller et al. (2014) found that NK cells from patients homozygous for the STX11 L58P mutation had defective lysis of K562 target cells.
checks.evidence_quote: All patients displayed defective lysis of K562 target cells and degranulation by NK cells in response to K562 target cells or engagement of the Fc receptor CD16 (Figures 1A,B).

checks.claim: NK cells from patients homozygous for the STX11 L58P mutation had defective degranulation in response to K562 cells or CD16 engagement.
checks.evidence_quote: All patients displayed defective lysis of K562 target cells and degranulation by NK cells in response to K562 target cells or engagement of the Fc receptor CD16 (Figures 1A,B).

checks.claim: Lysis and degranulation by NK cells from patients homozygous for STX11 L58P were partially restored by IL-2 stimulation.
checks.evidence_quote: Notably, cytotoxicity and degranulation were partially restored by IL-2 stimulation (Figures 1C,D).

checks.claim: Expression of perforin, granzyme B, and CD107a was normal in NK cells from patients homozygous for STX11 L58P, indicating that granule integrity was not impaired.
checks.evidence_quote: expression of cytotoxic granule constituents’ perforin, granzyme B, and CD107a was normal in patient NK cells, suggesting that granule integrity was not impaired (Figure 2).

checks.claim: In pull-down experiments, the patient-derived STX11 L58P mutation in the Habc domain abolished binding of syntaxin-11 to Munc18-2.
checks.evidence_quote: Notably, in pull-down experiments using beads loaded with FLAG-tagged Stx11 wild-type and Stx11 mutants neither FLAG-tagged Stx11 R4A nor L58P mutants bound HA-tagged Munc18-2 (Figure 4E).

checks.claim: In pull-down experiments, an engineered STX11 mutation in the N-terminal peptide (R4A) abolished binding of syntaxin-11 to Munc18-2.
checks.evidence_quote: Notably, in pull-down experiments using beads loaded with FLAG-tagged Stx11 wild-type and Stx11 mutants neither FLAG-tagged Stx11 R4A nor L58P mutants bound HA-tagged Munc18-2 (Figure 4E).
checks.explanation: R4A was generated by site-directed mutagenesis in the N-peptide.

checks.claim: In pull-down experiments, the C-terminal STX11 Q268X mutant still bound Munc18-2.
checks.evidence_quote: In contrast, the C-terminal Stx11 Q268X mutation previously associated with FHL4, did not display impaired binding of Munc18-2 (Figure 4E).

checks.claim: Muller et al. (2014) concluded that both the N terminus and the Habc domain of syntaxin-11 are needed to bind Munc18-2.
checks.evidence_quote: In conclusion, we demonstrate that both the N-terminus and Habc domain of Stx11 are involved in binding to Munc18-2.

checks.claim: Muller et al. (2014) suggested that loss of the syntaxin-11/Munc18-2 interaction may destabilize syntaxin-11 and explain the low levels of mutant syntaxin-11 protein in patient cells.
checks.evidence_quote: Thus, conversely, it is tenable that Stx11 mutations that disrupt Munc18-2 binding might reduce Stx11 expression through a similar mechanism, explaining the low expression of mutant Stx11 in patient cells.

paragraphs.text: Locatelli et al. (2020) conducted an open-label, single-group, phase 2-3 study of emapalumab, a human anti-interferon-gamma antibody, given with dexamethasone to 34 patients aged 18 years or younger with primary HLH (27 previously treated and 7 previously untreated). Of the previously treated patients, 63% responded, compared with the prespecified null hypothesis of 40% (P = 0.02); 65% of all patients who received emapalumab responded (P = 0.005). Seventy percent of the previously treated patients and 65% of all treated patients were able to proceed to transplantation. Emapalumab was not associated with organ toxicity. Severe infections developed in 10 patients during treatment, and emapalumab was discontinued in 1 patient because of disseminated histoplasmosis.

checks.claim: Locatelli et al. (2020) conducted an open-label, single-group, phase 2-3 study of emapalumab, a human anti-interferon-gamma antibody, given with dexamethasone.
checks.evidence_quote: We investigated the efficacy and safety of emapalumab (a human anti-interferon-γ antibody), administered with dexamethasone, in an open-label, single-group, phase 2-3 study
checks.explanation: The abstract states the study design and the drug exactly as the claim does.

checks.claim: The emapalumab study by Locatelli et al. (2020) included 34 patients aged 18 years or younger with primary HLH, 27 previously treated and 7 previously untreated.
checks.evidence_quote: a total of 34 patients (27 previously treated patients and 7 previously untreated patients) had received emapalumab
checks.explanation: The patient counts match. The Methods section of the abstract gives the age limit (18 years or younger) and the diagnosis (primary HLH).

checks.claim: In the Locatelli et al. (2020) study, 63% of previously treated primary HLH patients responded to emapalumab, compared with the prespecified null hypothesis of 40% (P = 0.02).
checks.evidence_quote: A total of 63% of the previously treated patients and 65% of the patients who received an emapalumab infusion had a response; these percentages were significantly higher than the prespecified null hypothesis of 40% (P = 0.02 and P = 0.005, respectively).
checks.explanation: The response rate (63%), the 40% null hypothesis and P = 0.02 all match the abstract.

checks.claim: In the Locatelli et al. (2020) study, 65% of all primary HLH patients who received emapalumab responded (P = 0.005).
checks.evidence_quote: 65% of the patients who received an emapalumab infusion had a response; these percentages were significantly higher than the prespecified null hypothesis of 40% (P = 0.02 and P = 0.005, respectively).
checks.explanation: The 65% response rate and P = 0.005 match the abstract.

checks.claim: In the Locatelli et al. (2020) study, 70% of previously treated patients and 65% of all emapalumab-treated patients were able to proceed to transplantation.
checks.evidence_quote: In the previously treated group, 70% of the patients were able to proceed to transplantation, as were 65% of the patients who received emapalumab.
checks.explanation: Both transplantation percentages match the abstract.

checks.claim: In the Locatelli et al. (2020) study, emapalumab was not associated with organ toxicity.
checks.evidence_quote: Emapalumab was not associated with any organ toxicity.

checks.claim: In the Locatelli et al. (2020) study, severe infections developed in 10 patients during emapalumab treatment.
checks.evidence_quote: Severe infections developed in 10 patients during emapalumab treatment.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly, including the count of 10 patients.

checks.claim: In the Locatelli et al. (2020) study, emapalumab was discontinued in 1 patient because of disseminated histoplasmosis.
checks.evidence_quote: Emapalumab was discontinued in 1 patient because of disseminated histoplasmosis.

paragraphs.text: Zur Stadt et al. (2006) found STX11 mutations in 6 of 32 Turkish patients with FHL but in none of 23 German patients or 8 patients of other origins. Rudd et al. (2006) found STX11 mutations in 14% of PRF1-negative FHL families in their cohort.

checks.claim: Zur Stadt et al. (2006) found STX11 mutations in 6 of 32 Turkish patients with FHL.
checks.evidence_quote: Of 32 patients from Turkey, 14 had mutations in PRF1, six had mutations in UNC13D, and six had mutations in STX11.
checks.explanation: 6 of 32 Turkish patients had STX11 mutations.

checks.claim: Zur Stadt et al. (2006) found no STX11 mutations in 23 German FHL patients or in 8 FHL patients of other origins.
checks.evidence_quote: three of 23 and four of 23 patients from Germany, and three of eight and two of eight from other origins showed mutations in PRF1 and UNC13D, respectively, but none in STX11.
checks.explanation: None of the 23 German patients or 8 patients of other origins had STX11 mutations.

checks.claim: Rudd et al. (2006) found STX11 mutations in 14% of PRF1-negative FHL families in their cohort.
checks.evidence_quote: STX11 gene mutations were found in 14% of the PRF1 negative FHL families included in the present cohort.

clinical_synopsis.feature: Defective natural killer cell cytotoxicity and degranulation
Onset in infancy or childhood (1 to 84 months)
Severe psychomotor retardation in some patients

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a large consanguineous Kurdish kindred with FHL4, zur Stadt et al. (2005) identified a homozygous 5-bp deletion in the STX11 gene. Syntaxin-11 protein was absent from the mononuclear cell fraction of patients homozygous for the deletion. The same homozygous deletion was found in 2 other consanguineous Turkish/Kurdish FHL kindreds.

checks.claim: zur Stadt et al. (2005) identified a homozygous 5-bp deletion in the STX11 gene in affected members of a large consanguineous Kurdish kindred with FHL4.
checks.evidence_quote: we identified a homozygous deletion of 5 bp in the syntaxin 11 gene (STX11) in this family

checks.claim: Syntaxin-11 protein was absent from the mononuclear cell fraction of patients homozygous for the 5-bp STX11 deletion.
checks.evidence_quote: syntaxin 11 protein was absent in the mononuclear cell fraction of patients with the homozygous 5 bp deletion

checks.claim: The homozygous 5-bp STX11 deletion was found in 2 other consanguineous Turkish/Kurdish FHL kindreds.
checks.evidence_quote: we found homozygous mutations in STX11 in five consanguineous Turkish/Kurdish FHL kindreds including two families with the 5 bp deletion

paragraphs.text: In a consanguineous Turkish/Kurdish kindred with FHL4, zur Stadt et al. (2005) identified a homozygous 19.2-kb genomic deletion spanning the entire coding region of STX11 (exon 2).

checks.claim: zur Stadt et al. (2005) identified a homozygous 19.2-kb genomic deletion spanning the entire coding region of STX11 (exon 2) in a consanguineous Turkish/Kurdish kindred with FHL4.
checks.evidence_quote: we found homozygous mutations in STX11 in five consanguineous Turkish/Kurdish FHL kindreds including two families with the 5 bp deletion, one family with a large 19.2 kb genomic deletion spanning the entire coding region of STX11 (exon 2)

paragraphs.text: Muller et al. (2014) found that the C-terminal Q268X mutant, unlike the N-terminal L58P mutant, did not impair binding of syntaxin-11 to Munc18-2 in transfected HEK293T cells.

checks.claim: Muller et al. (2014) found that the C-terminal STX11 Q268X mutant did not impair binding of syntaxin-11 to Munc18-2 in transfected HEK293T cells.
checks.evidence_quote: In contrast, the C-terminal Stx11 Q268X mutation previously associated with FHL4, did not display impaired binding of Munc18-2 (Figure 4E).

checks.claim: Muller et al. (2014) found that the N-terminal STX11 L58P mutant impaired binding of syntaxin-11 to Munc18-2 in transfected HEK293T cells.
checks.evidence_quote: biochemical analyses examining ectopically expressed, tagged Stx11 in a cell line revealed that the Stx11 L58P mutation disrupted interactions with tagged Munc18-2.
checks.explanation: HEK-293T cells; L58P is in the N-terminal Habc domain.

paragraphs.text: In 3 patients with FHL4 from 3 unrelated consanguineous Pakistani families, Muller et al. (2014) identified a homozygous c.173T-C transition in the STX11 gene, resulting in a leu58-to-pro (L58P) substitution in an alpha-helix of the N-terminal Habc domain. The parents were heterozygous for the mutation. Patient NK cells had defective cytotoxicity and degranulation, and syntaxin-11 expression was greatly reduced in patient PBMCs and LAK cells. In transfected HEK293T cells, the mutant protein was expressed at levels similar to wildtype but did not bind Munc18-2.

checks.claim: Muller et al. (2014) identified a homozygous c.173T-C transition in the STX11 gene in 3 patients with FHL4 from 3 unrelated consanguineous Pakistani families.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified a homozygous STX11 mutation, c.173T > C (p.L58P), in three patients presenting clinically with hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis from unrelated Pakistani families.
checks.explanation: Table 1 shows consanguinity in all three families.

checks.claim: The STX11 c.173T-C transition results in a leu58-to-pro (L58P) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: STX11 | 173T > C, Leu58Pro hmz

checks.claim: The STX11 L58P substitution lies in an alpha-helix of the N-terminal Habc domain of syntaxin-11.
checks.evidence_quote: The L58P localizes to an α-helical strand of the predicted Stx11 Habc domain.
checks.explanation: Abstract calls the Habc domain N-terminal.

checks.claim: The parents of the 3 Pakistani FHL4 patients were heterozygous for the STX11 L58P mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: The parents were heterozygous for this STX11 mutation, but did not have any recorded history of inflammatory disease.

checks.claim: NK cells from the Pakistani patients homozygous for STX11 L58P had defective cytotoxicity and degranulation.
checks.evidence_quote: NK cell activitya | Deficient | Deficient | Deficient
checks.explanation: Degranulation was also deficient in all three.

checks.claim: Syntaxin-11 expression was greatly reduced in PBMCs and LAK cells from patients homozygous for STX11 L58P.
checks.evidence_quote: LAK cells from the patient also displayed a selective loss of Stx11 expression, whereas Munc18-2 expression was similar to that of control LAK cells (Figure 3B).
checks.explanation: Expression was analyzed only in patient C, not in 'patients' plural.

checks.claim: In transfected HEK293T cells, the STX11 L58P mutant protein was expressed at levels similar to wildtype.
checks.evidence_quote: In transfection experiments, both Stx11 R4A and L58P mutants were expressed at levels comparable to Stx11 wild-type (Figure 4D).

checks.claim: In transfected HEK293T cells, the STX11 L58P mutant protein did not bind Munc18-2.
checks.evidence_quote: neither FLAG-tagged Stx11 R4A nor L58P mutants bound HA-tagged Munc18-2 (Figure 4E).
